source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: define prefill/decode ownership, KV placement and eviction, RDMA transfer cost, cache consistency, admission control, failure recovery, and comparison against local or conventional distributed serving. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Treat Mooncake-style KV disaggregation in variant -49476 as a testable design choice, not an assumed benefit. Assume a long-context multi-node service, but first inventory model and runtime versions, GPU/NIC types, PCIe and NUMA topology, link capacity, memory limits, and failure domains; label unknowns rather than inventing platform facts. Assign prefill workers prompt computation and decode workers token generation, then specify KV block shape and precision, ownership, placement, replication, eviction/TTL, version or checksum validation, batching, concurrency, admission limits, migration, and behavior for stale or partial blocks.

Falsifiable hypothesis: at a pre-registered offered load and prompt/output distribution, remote KV placement improves throughput or p99 inter-token latency by a stated margin versus a colocated/local-KV or conventional distributed baseline, while meeting TTFT, error, freshness, and recovery SLOs. Keep model, sampling, traffic mix, warm-up, cache state, batching, concurrency, and admission policy matched. Measure TTFT, inter-token and end-to-end latency, requests/s, tokens/s, queueing, KV hit/miss/eviction, RDMA bytes and transfer milliseconds, retries/timeouts, GPU/NIC/PCIe/CPU utilization, memory, and synchronized p50/p95/p99 values with units, repetitions, and uncertainty. Attribute RDMA transfer separately from compute, serialization, queueing, and cache-miss costs; control for cache warmth, topology, load skew, compression, and background traffic.

Validate request identity, KV version/checksum consistency, output equivalence, tenant isolation, bounded retries, and absence of stale-block use. Fault-test cache-worker, compute-node, link, and control-plane loss: drain or replicate safely, invalidate affected entries, re-fetch or recompute from an authorized source, bound fallback to local KV/recompute, and avoid silent corruption. Apply admission backpressure or rejection before memory exhaustion. Roll back when latency, error, freshness, correctness, or recovery thresholds fail, or when RDMA is unavailable; preserve only authorized telemetry and protect request/KV data. Claim improvement only after topology, implementation behavior, matched controls, and fault evidence are available.

Assume a long-context multi-node service, but first inventory model and runtime versions, GPU/NIC types, PCIe and NUMA topology, link capacity, memory limits, and failure domains; label unknowns rather than inventing platform facts. Assign prefill workers prompt computation and decode workers token generation, then specify KV block shape and precision, ownership, placement, replication, eviction/TTL, version or checksum validation, batching, concurrency, admission limits, migration, and behavior for stale or partial blocks.

Falsifiable hypothesis: at a pre-registered offered load and prompt/output distribution, remote KV placement improves throughput or p99 inter-token latency by a stated margin versus a colocated/local-KV or conventional distributed baseline, while meeting TTFT, error, freshness, and recovery SLOs. Keep model, sampling, traffic mix, warm-up, cache state, batching, concurrency, and admission policy matched. Measure TTFT, inter-token and end-to-end latency, requests/s, tokens/s, queueing, KV hit/miss/eviction, RDMA bytes and transfer milliseconds, retries/timeouts, GPU/NIC/PCIe/CPU utilization, memory, and synchronized p50/p95/p99 values with units, repetitions, and uncertainty. Attribute RDMA transfer separately from compute, serialization, queueing, and cache-miss costs; control for cache warmth, topology, load skew, compression, and background traffic.

Validate request identity, KV version/checksum consistency, output equivalence, tenant isolation, bounded retries, and absence of stale-block use. Fault-test cache-worker, compute-node, link, and control-plane loss: drain or replicate safely, invalidate affected entries, re-fetch or recompute from an authorized source, bound fallback to local KV/recompute, and avoid silent corruption. Apply admission backpressure or rejection before memory exhaustion. Roll back when latency, error, freshness, correctness, or recovery thresholds fail, or when RDMA is unavailable; preserve only authorized telemetry and protect request/KV data. Claim improvement only after topology, implementation behavior, matched controls, and fault evidence are available.

quality_dimensions.coverage: mechanisms, boundaries, failure modes, measurement plan, assumptions, and safety limits
quality_dimensions.falsifiability: pre-registered baseline, margin, metrics, and rollback gates
quality_dimensions.measurement_plan: units, percentiles, synchronized timestamps, controls, variability, and confounders

risks: RDMA, Mooncake semantics, topology, and recovery behavior are environment-dependent and unverified
remote KV may add transfer, queueing, stale-data, privacy, or memory-pressure risk
synthetic rubric is not authoritative domain review
evidence_required: read-only topology and software inventory
matched local/conventional baseline and controlled workload
RDMA and KV placement/version/eviction telemetry
repeated measurements with uncertainty
fault-injection results for cache, node, link, and control-plane loss
authorized correctness, isolation, and recovery validation
